Series::isclose¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::isclose(const Series& other) const
Series Series::isclose(const Series& other, double rtol, double atol) const
Series Series::isclose(const Series& other, double rtol, double atol, bool equal_nan) const

What It Does¶

Broadcasts the two operands and returns a Bool Series marking, per position, whether the values agree within a tolerance.

For a receiver value a and a reference value b, the rule is:

close  iff  a == b                              (exact equality wins first)
       or   |a - b| <= atol + rtol * |b|        (and both a, b finite)

Two consequences of that first line: exactly-equal finite values are always close regardless of tolerance, and matching infinities (+inf vs +inf, -inf vs -inf) are close — but opposite infinities are not, because |inf - (-inf)| is not finite.

The tolerance has two terms because a single one never fits everywhere: rtol * |b| scales with the magnitude being compared (good for large numbers), and atol is a fixed floor that takes over near zero, where rtol * |b| shrinks to almost nothing. The defaults are rtol = 1e-5, atol = 1e-8.

Because rtol multiplies |b| — the other operand — the relation is not symmetric. a.isclose(b) and b.isclose(a) can disagree near the boundary. Choose the reference deliberately.

isclose gives you the mask — where the comparison fails. To reduce it to one bool, use allclose.

Parameters¶

other (const Series&): the reference values. Must have the same dtype and platform as self, and a broadcast-compatible shape. (This is stricter than equal, which tolerates differing dtype.)

rtol (double): nonnegative relative tolerance, multiplied by |other|.

atol (double): nonnegative absolute floor. Dominates near zero.

equal_nan (bool, default false): when true, positions where both operands are NaN are marked close. A NaN is never close to a finite value or to an infinity.

Returns¶

Series A Bool Series of the broadcast shape, true where the pair is close.

Raises¶

  • if the dtypes differ, or the platforms differ

  • if rtol < 0 or atol < 0

  • if the shapes are not broadcast-compatible

Gradient¶

isclose is a predicate — its Bool result carries no useful derivative across the comparison boundary.

Examples¶

Example 1. Same shape, one value inside the default tolerance and one outside.

auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
auto b = pluss::make_series({1.0 + 1e-9, 2.0 + 1e-3, 3.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.isclose(b));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, true]

Position 0 is off by 1e-9 — well inside atol + rtol*|b| ≈ 1e-8 + 2e-5. Position 1 is off by 1e-3, far outside. Position 2 is exactly equal.

Example 2. Relative tolerance is directional.

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "9 close to 10: "
          << pluss::make_series({9.0}).isclose(pluss::make_series({10.0}), 0.1, 0.0).item<bool>() << "\n"
          << "10 close to 9: "
          << pluss::make_series({10.0}).isclose(pluss::make_series({9.0}), 0.1, 0.0).item<bool>() << "\n";

Output¶

9 close to 10: true
10 close to 9: false

The allowance in the first call is 0.1 * |10| = 1, and the error is exactly 1 — it passes. Reversed, the allowance is 0.1 * |9| = 0.9, too small.

Example 3. Broadcasting turns isclose into a comparison grid — its main use over allclose is seeing where things diverge.

auto a = pluss::make_series({9.0, 20.0}).reshape({2, 1});
auto b = pluss::make_series({{10.0, 20.0, 40.0}});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.isclose(b, 0.1, 0.0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡  true false false ⎤
⎣ false  true false ⎦

The [2, 1] receiver and [1, 3] reference broadcast to [2, 3]; each cell is one isclose check.

Example 4. Near zero, atol carries the comparison — rtol alone vanishes.

auto a = pluss::make_series({0.0, 0.0});
auto b = pluss::make_series({1e-9, 1e-3});
std::cout << "rtol only (atol=0): ";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.isclose(b, 1e-5, 0.0));
std::cout << "default atol=1e-8:  ";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.isclose(b));

Output¶

rtol only (atol=0): Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[false, false]default atol=1e-8:  Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false]

With atol = 0 the allowance at b = 1e-9 is 1e-5 * 1e-9 ≈ 1e-14 — even a 1e-9 gap fails. The default atol = 1e-8 lets the first pair through (1e-9 <= 1e-8) while the 1e-3 gap still fails. This is why you almost always want a nonzero atol when values can approach zero.

Example 5. Exact equality is checked first — matching infinities pass, and rtol = atol = 0 gives a pure exact comparison.

double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
auto a = pluss::make_series({inf, -inf, 5.0});
auto b = pluss::make_series({inf, inf, 5.0});
std::cout << "matching +inf, opposite inf, equal finite: ";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.isclose(b));

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0000001});
auto y = pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0});
std::cout << "rtol=atol=0 (pure exact): ";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.isclose(y, 0.0, 0.0));

Output¶

matching +inf, opposite inf, equal finite: Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, true]rtol=atol=0 (pure exact): Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false]

+inf vs +inf → true (exact). +inf vs -inf → false (|inf + inf| is not finite). With both tolerances zero, isclose reduces to elementwise exact equality — like eq, but still subject to the dtype-match requirement.

Example 6. NaN and infinity, with and without equal_nan.

double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
double nan = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
auto a = pluss::make_series({inf, -inf, nan, 1.0});
auto b = pluss::make_series({inf, inf, nan, 1.000001});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.isclose(b)) << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.isclose(b, 1e-5, 1e-8, true));

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, false, true]
Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, true, true]

equal_nan = true flips only position 2 (both NaN); -inf vs +inf stays false.

Example 7. Contract violations fail before any comparison.

try {
  pluss::make_series({1.0}).isclose(pluss::make_series({1}));   // float vs int
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  pluss::make_series({1.0}).isclose(pluss::make_series({1.0}), -1.0, 0.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

isclose: receiver and other must have the same dtype
isclose: rtol must be greater than or equal to zero

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Not symmetric. rtol scales |other|, so a.isclose(b) and b.isclose(a) can differ near the boundary — pick the reference operand deliberately.

  • atol matters near zero. With atol = 0, values close to zero almost never pass, because rtol * |b| collapses. Keep a nonzero atol for data that can be near zero.

  • Dtype must match exactly — unlike equal. Convert one side with to first. Integer/Bool inputs are promoted to Float32 internally for the arithmetic, but only after the dtype-equality check.

  • Opposite infinities are never close; matching infinities always are.

  • NaN is close only to a paired NaN, and only with equal_nan = true.

Summary¶

isclose(other, rtol = 1e-5, atol = 1e-8, equal_nan = false) is the per-position tolerant comparison:

  • close iff exactly equal, or |a - b| <= atol + rtol*|b| with both finite

  • exact equality (and matching infinities) always pass; opposite infinities never do

  • asymmetric — rtol scales the other operand

  • requires identical dtype (stricter than equal)

  • reduce to one bool with allclose

See Also¶

  • Series::allclose: reduce this mask to one bool.

  • Series::equal: exact whole-tensor comparison, no broadcasting, dtype-tolerant.

  • Series::eq: exact elementwise comparison (isclose with both tolerances 0, minus the dtype check nuance).
